name: jira_issue_create
description: jira.issue.create (write; approval: approve). Submit human names (project, issue type, transition, user, link type, parent page); the app resolves and validates them. Do not pre-read createmeta, transitions or assignable users; if you need metadata, fetch it in one script. Text in `fields`, `update` and `comment` is sent as Jira wiki markup unchanged; only `description`/`body` with `body_format=markdown` are converted. Result shapes: ops_describe.

fields.description: Extra Jira fields in REST shape, keyed by system field id or customfield_N; a key that duplicates a dedicated param is rejected.

expected.description: {field id: value as read}; a mismatch at enrichment puts the request in the conflict state. Recommended for every edited field, especially description.

description: jira.worklog.add (write; approval: approve). Submit human names (project, issue type, transition, user, link type, parent page); the app resolves and validates them. Do not pre-read createmeta, transitions or assignable users; if you need metadata, fetch it in one script. Text in `fields`, `update` and `comment` is sent as Jira wiki markup unchanged; only `description`/`body` with `body_format=markdown` are converted. Result shapes: ops_describe.

comment.description: Plain text or Jira wiki markup, sent as written (not converted from Markdown). The preview lists its macros, mentions and links.

started.description: Jira timestamp yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ with the zone as +hhmm, e.g. 2026-09-02T09:00:00.000+0200. Exactly 3 millisecond digits, a zone of +hhmm or -hhmm up to 1400 (not Z, not +hh:mm), year 2000 or later; the date is not checked against any clock, the preview shows the UTC instant. Omitted: Jira uses the time the worklog is created.

time_spent.description: Time as Jira reads timeSpent: amounts of w, d, h, m separated by single spaces, largest first, each unit once (1w 2d 3h 30m). Each amount has 1 to 4 digits. More than zero, at most 4w (160h, 9600m). w and d are working time (Jira default 1d = 8h, 1w = 5d; the instance decides). No seconds, no decimals, no 2h30m.

name: jira_issuelink_create
description: jira.issuelink.create (write; approval: approve). Submit human names (project, issue type, transition, user, link type, parent page); the app resolves and validates them. Do not pre-read createmeta, transitions or assignable users; if you need metadata, fetch it in one script. Text in `fields`, `update` and `comment` is sent as Jira wiki markup unchanged; only `description`/`body` with `body_format=markdown` are converted. Result shapes: ops_describe.

inward.description: Issue the link starts from (sent as inwardIssue): it gets the type's outward phrase, e.g. with type Blocks this issue blocks outward.

outward.description: Issue the outward phrase points at (sent as outwardIssue), e.g. with type Blocks this issue is blocked by inward.

type.description: Link type name (or id, or one of its phrases); the app resolves it. A phrase never changes the direction: the link always reads from inward to outward with the type's outward phrase.

name: jira_sprint_move_issues
description: jira.sprint.move_issues (write; approval: approve). Submit human names (project, issue type, transition, user, link type, parent page); the app resolves and validates them. Do not pre-read createmeta, transitions or assignable users; if you need metadata, fetch it in one script. Text in `fields`, `update` and `comment` is sent as Jira wiki markup unchanged; only `description`/`body` with `body_format=markdown` are converted. Result shapes: ops_describe.

id.description: Sprint id (as jira.sprint.list lists it). The app reads the sprint first: the move can be approved only into a future or active sprint; a closed sprint holds it (deny only).

issues.description: Issue keys to move, 1 to 50, each listed once (ABC-01 and ABC-1 are one issue), at most 255 characters each. More than 50 is refused: split into requests of ≤ 50 issues; moves of disjoint issues can be batch-approved.

issues.description: Issue keys to move to the backlog (each issue leaves its future and active sprints), 1 to 50, each listed once (ABC-01 and ABC-1 are one issue), at most 255 characters each. More than 50 is refused: split into requests of ≤ 50 issues; moves of disjoint issues can be batch-approved.

name: confluence_page_create
description: confluence.page.create (write; approval: approve). Submit human names (project, issue type, transition, user, link type, parent page); the app resolves and validates them. Do not pre-read createmeta, transitions or assignable users; if you need metadata, fetch it in one script. A Markdown body that still contains `page get` placeholders (`[macro: …]`, `confluence:` links or images, `@user:<key>`) is rejected with `markdown_placeholders`: fetch with `--format storage` and submit `body_format=storage`. Result shapes: ops_describe.

parent.description: Parent page id or title (same space); a value of digits only is always a page id.

name: confluence_page_update
description: confluence.page.update (write; approval: approve). Submit human names (project, issue type, transition, user, link type, parent page); the app resolves and validates them. Do not pre-read createmeta, transitions or assignable users; if you need metadata, fetch it in one script. A Markdown body that still contains `page get` placeholders (`[macro: …]`, `confluence:` links or images, `@user:<key>`) is rejected with `markdown_placeholders`: fetch with `--format storage` and submit `body_format=storage`. If `page get` reported `meta.conversion.lossy = true`, edit with `body_format=storage`; a Markdown update that would remove macros (task lists included), images or links (mentions included) is flagged to the approver. Result shapes: ops_describe.

examples.body: Release 1.4 fixes the login and the reset flow.

base_version.description: The version number you read; the app sends base_version + 1 and flags a newer server version as a conflict.

name: script_run
description: Run a read-only script in the sandbox; the user approves only the final result. Run every new or changed script with dry_run sparse and dry_run full first (no approval needed; results come from documented examples, meta.dry_run: true), then run it for real once. Default limits: heap_mb=256, max_call_result_mb=16, max_calls=200, max_concurrent_calls=4, max_fetch_mb=50, max_result_mb=16, process_mb=512, timeout_s=120; the effective limits for an instance: ops_describe with op_id and instance (field script_limits).

name: request_await
description: Wait for a request's decision (up to ATLAS_DUCK_MCP_TIMEOUT). Never resubmit a pending request.

name: request_status
description: Report where a request stands. Never blocks and never returns data.

name: request_cancel
description: Cancel a request by id. Only this tool cancels: dropping or cancelling a tool call never does.

name: request_list
description: List pending or recent requests. Metadata only; recover a lost id with match_params.

name: ops_list
description: List the operations with class, approval and description.

name: ops_describe
description: Describe one operation: params schema, result shapes, caps and script_limits (effective with an instance).

description: List the configured instances.
